result:
result: Not blocking. The three commits are correct on Linux, the new tests fail on the base, and both gates pass. I could not run the Windows which test.
changed: none (read-only; scratch copy of e6f334c7 under the scratchpad)
checks:
- `bunx --no-install mise run build` -> exit 0, `git status --short` empty before and after.
- `bunx --no-install mise run verify` -> exit 0 at 1b9dee14. Type-check had no errors in 282 files, lint had no problems in 283 files, and the format check passed 696 files. Tests: 3065 pass, 0 fail, 102 files. The working tree was clean afterwards.
- Base check: I ran the new `devices.test.ts` against e6f334c7's `devices.ts`. About 40 tests fail there, covering aliases, links, `/dev` removal, cp from a missing or folder source, and ENOTDIR. All pass on the head.
- The Git-folder test needs `ProgramW6432` and the per-user `Programs\Git\cmd` folder, which the base lacks.

blockers: none

notes (all optional; the built-in `/code-review` ran as itself, and I read the code behind each of its findings):
- Performance: each guarded call now makes 1 to 3 extra `realpath` calls, including `MountableFs` routing on Windows. A lexical prefilter cannot catch links, so I would measure before changing it.
- The guard is check-then-act, so two concurrent calls could race. It is best effort and tests cannot pin it.
- `/dev/null/.` and `/dev/null/..` do not get ENOTDIR. This is a cosmetic edge; the guard still never reaches the host device.
- `cp -r dir /dev/null` returns EISDIR where real cp errors differently. Edge case.
- `followed` duplicates `real`'s `tryPromise` and map logic and could be built from it.
- `ProgramFiles(x86)` is not searched, and `ProgramW6432` duplicates `ProgramFiles` on 64-bit hosts. The test asserts the duplicate is collapsed, so there is no extra scan.
- No test pins the new order of `withNullDevice` below `withProgramLaunch`. The comment in `shell.ts` explains why, and the bash-shell tests pass.
- Relative paths are classified as elsewhere. Interpreter calls use absolute paths, so I did not treat this as a defect.

evidence:
The device guard, the which test and the Git search folders behave as claimed, with tests that fail without them: `devices.test.ts` run on the e6f334c7 source gives about 40 `(fail)` lines and passes on the head. The which test uses `HOST.toLowerCase()`, the bun that sits in the call's PATH. The Windows log (win-106b.txt:3389-3403) shows only `/usr/bin/git` was missing, and `cat` was found. I could not run Windows here, so the `/usr/bin/bun` result there is read, not run.
No regression in the just-bash shell or host passthrough, and no test is weakened or skipped on Windows: `verify` runs 3065 pass, 0 fail. No `skip` or Windows exclusions were added. The one loosening is the passthrough mock in bash-shell.test.ts, where `realpath` and `stat` calls are filtered out of the `seen` list. It still asserts that `writeFile /tmp/copy` is the only call that goes through.
Gates: mise run build leaves the tree unchanged and mise run verify exits 0 at 1b9dee14: build exit 0 with a clean `git status`; verify exit 0 with 3065 pass and 0 fail. Logs are at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-holyagent/43946df6-456d-58c6-bea3-7e958fcb9495/scratchpad/rv-build.txt and rv-verify.txt.
